official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification — positional accuracy validation and checkpoints
official_sources.finding: Absolute and relative vertical accuracy must be verified before derivative production; checkpoints must be independent from calibration control, located within the data production area, stratified for NVA and VVA, and accompanied by detailed validation evidence.
official_sources.limitation: Project-level checkpoint validation does not establish the error of a specific parcel extrema pair without spatially relevant support and matching immutable source lineage.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification glossary — checkpoint, control point and well-distributed
official_sources.finding: A checkpoint is an independent surveyed point from a source of greater accuracy, control points cannot also serve as checkpoints, and well-distributed checkpoints require spacing and quadrant coverage rules.
official_sources.limitation: The rectangular-area distribution heuristic must be adapted explicitly for irregular parcel or project geometry and cannot be applied mechanically.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification tables — land-cover classes and vertical-accuracy thresholds
official_sources.finding: The specification separates relative precision, nonvegetated RMSEv requirements, land-cover reporting classes and quality-level thresholds.
official_sources.limitation: A listed quality-level threshold is a dataset acceptance criterion, not a substitute for observed checkpoint residuals or parcel-specific uncertainty.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification deliverables — survey point and QA/QC evidence
official_sources.finding: Checkpoint deliverables must retain the survey point set, CRS, source geoid, horizontal and vertical references, units, source coordinates, elevation, point accuracy and QA/QC assessment materials.
official_sources.limitation: Presence of attributes does not prove their correctness; every field must be validated and bound to the source file digest.

official_sources.title: USGS Survey Point Delivery requirements
official_sources.finding: The delivered GeoPackage must contain all checkpoints actually used in final vertical-accuracy assessment, use the lidar CRS and retain standardized survey-point attribution.
official_sources.limitation: A complete delivery ledger still requires proof that no excluded or substituted points influenced the reported statistics.

official_sources.title: USGS 3DEP vertical accuracy error dictionary
official_sources.finding: USGS quality review treats non-well-distributed survey points and survey-point defects as explicit vertical-accuracy errors.
official_sources.limitation: An error dictionary identifies review failures but does not calculate corrected residuals or uncertainty.

official_sources.title: NIST residual lag-plot independence assessment
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Residual dependence can bias estimated error standard deviation and lead to improper inference; lag plots are used to detect structure rather than assuming independence.
official_sources.limitation: A one-dimensional lag plot does not fully characterize two-dimensional spatial autocorrelation; spatial ordering and neighborhood definitions must be declared.

official_sources.title: NIST detection and treatment of potential outliers
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Potential outliers must be labeled and investigated; they may reflect bad data, random variation or scientifically meaningful behavior and should not be automatically deleted without an evidence-based disposition.
official_sources.limitation: Distribution-specific outlier tests require their assumptions to be checked and cannot justify post-hoc removal merely to improve RMSE.
